process_steps.input_state: master alloy with raw elemental metal purity > 99.5 wt%

evidence.quote: To obtain tensile samples, the CrFeNi2V0.5W0.25 alloy ingot (100 g) was produced by high-frequency induction melting furnace. The BN crucible and graphite crucible were preheated at 200 °C ... In all cases, the furnace chamber was first evacuated to 5×10−3 Pa and then backfilled with high-purity argon gas to reach 0.05 MPa.
It can be observed that the CrFeNi2V0.5 alloy exhibited a single-FCC-phase solid solution structure. The lattice parameter of FCC phase was 3.5892 Å
A columnar grain microstructure with a grains width of around 100 μm was determined by the linear intercept method.
The CrFeNi2V0.5W0.25 alloy possessed a main FCC solid solution structure with the lattice parameter of a = 3.6329 Å
and a few FeCr-type σ phases (Pearson Symbol tP30, a = b = 8.800 Å, c = 4.544 Å, c/a = 0.52,)

attributes.size: larger dendritic region, smaller interdendritic region

evidence.quote: the alloy exhibited a typical dendritic morphology, and the larger dendritic region (denoted as DR) has a single phase and the smaller interdendritic region (denoted as IR) has an eutectic microstructure.
the smaller interdendritic region (denoted as IR) has an eutectic microstructure.
It can be found that high-density dislocations and dislocation wall were observed in FCC phase.
On the fracture surface, a high density of dimple-like features can be obviously observed, which may suggest the microvoid coalescence mode fracture.
A lot of slip lines (indicated by the white arrow in Fig. 4a) were found in the dendritic region with FCC structure
In addition, cast void is observed as well, and the crack always initiates from a cast void.

conditions.test_method: uniaxial compression test on cylindrical samples

evidence.quote: the CrFeNi2V0.5W0.25 alloy has a higher yield strength (σy) of 278 MPa than that of the W-free alloy (σy= 78 MPa)

conditions.test_method: uniaxial compression test on cylindrical samples

evidence.quote: the CrFeNi2V0.5W0.25 alloy has a higher yield strength (σy) of 278 MPa than that of the W-free alloy (σy= 78 MPa)
Both alloys demonstrated significant capability of strain and better ductility (ε > 70%), which is higher than most reported values.

evidence.quote: From the engineering stress–strain curve, the yield strength, fracture strength, and elongation were 343 MPa, 640 MPa, and 15.7%, respectively.
The higher strength of CrFeNi2V0.5W0.25 alloy is predominantly due to the solid solution strengthening of W element and σ phase precipitation strengthening.

The tensile deformation mode of the FCC phase in the CrFeNi2V0.5W0.25 alloy is dominated by planar glide, relating to dislocation configurations, high-density dislocations, and dislocation wall.
Therefore, dislocation slip plays a significant role in tensile deformation of CrFeNi2V0.5W0.25 high-entropy alloy.
